case_payload.fixed_engineering_facts: Source-derived scenario (Table A3, PDF page 13): frequency B, severity IV, Moderate risk. Listed safeguards are PSV-101 A/B and PAHH-102 with closing action on SDV-30010. The source recommends reassessing and reactivating the platform well shutdown and safety system. Synthetic decision-model assumptions: the fixed cost is in arbitrary normalized units, not a source-derived price. The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. Functional testing in the proposal is an experimental implementation detail, not a reported performance test from the article. A demand means a call for the reactivated platform well shutdown and safety function in the higher-pressure scenario. Success means delivery of the intended shutdown and safety action within the specified function scope. There are exactly two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes per demand: successful delivery of this specified function, or unavailability of this function. For this exercise, unavailability means that the specified function is not successfully delivered on demand, including failure to perform it; this is an operational definition, not a general equivalence of reliability and availability. The decision concerns the next 100 eligible demands after the proposed action is in place; their occurrence rate is not specified. Reliability applies only to this function and does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk.
case_payload.proposal: Reactivate and functionally test the platform well shutdown and safety system associated with the higher-pressure scenario.
case_payload.title: Reactivation of the platform well shutdown and safety system

condition_payload.manipulation_text: Reliability assessment: the specified function will be unavailable on 5 of 100 demands.

surface_form_payload.question_text: Should management approve this safeguard recommendation?

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP basis: the node is V-001 and associated lines (CASE-01). The design intent, implied rather than stated, is to receive and separate crude within the pressure envelope of the input line and V-001. Guideword MORE applied to PRESSURE gives an overpressure deviation (CASE-02). The packet supplies no cause or consequence detail. The source ranks the scenario frequency B / severity IV = Moderate. It credits PSV-101 A/B (relief) and PAHH-102 closing SDV-30010 (isolation), and itself recommends reassessing and reactivating the platform well shutdown and safety system (CASE-03). Reliability: each demand has two mutually exclusive, exhaustive outcomes. 'Unavailable on 5 of 100 demands' therefore equals 'delivered on 95 of 100 demands' (P_success 0.95, P_unavailable 0.05). Over the next 100 eligible demands, expect ~95 successful shutdown/safety actions and ~5 unavailabilities. The loss wording adds no information, and facts and cost are frame-invariant (CASE-04). Judgment: the proposal implements the source recommendation and includes functional testing to verify the function on reactivation. By its designation, the restored well-level layer acts at the supply end rather than duplicating the vessel-level PAHH/SDV and PSV layers. Existing safeguards are not removed and remain as backup on the ~5% of demands where the function is unavailable. The action therefore adds defence in depth for a Moderate-ranked scenario. The fixed 100-unit normalized cost has no stated budget constraint or better alternative, so there is no stated basis to reject or defer. Recommendation: approve, with four conditions: MOC review of why the system was deactivated (implied by 'reactivate'); verification of independence from PAHH-102/SDV-30010; a defined proof-test interval; and re-ranking of residual risk after implementation. The 95% figure is stipulated function reliability, not a quantified accident-prevention claim.

Records the source recommendation to reassess and reactivate the platform well shutdown and safety system. Gives the operational definitions (two exhaustive outcomes per demand, stipulated reliability, normalized cost, unspecified demand rate) used to read 5/100 unavailability as 95/100 success.

The 95% per-demand success (5% unavailability) is experimentally stipulated, not source-derived. Proof-test interval, test coverage and degradation across the 100-demand window are not provided.

Independence of the platform well shutdown and safety system from PAHH-102/SDV-30010 and PSV-101 A/B is not stated (for example shared sensors, logic, final elements or utilities). Common-cause failure could reduce the added benefit.

The packet does not give the initiating causes of the higher-pressure deviation, the specific consequence behind severity IV, or the direction of the source severity scale. Only the source 'Moderate' ranking is relied on.
Cost is in arbitrary normalized units with no budget limit, benefit valuation or competing alternative, so cost-effectiveness cannot be quantified.
The packet does not say why the well shutdown and safety system is currently inactive, nor describe its exact shutdown actions and scope. Reactivation should pass management-of-change review.

The stated reliability covers only delivery of the specified function. It does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk, so post-implementation risk must be re-ranked rather than assumed.
The current condition and demonstrated performance of PSV-101 A/B and PAHH-102/SDV-30010 are not provided.
